entries.what: A banjo in the subtractive tradition: tremolo at about 10 Hz, a low-pass cutoff around 2900 Hz, no resonance, the envelope opening the filter by about 75%.
entries.why: These are the settings a synthesis teacher chose to make this instrument recognisable, which makes them a demonstrated starting point rather than a preference. What carries the identification is usually the combination rather than any one value: the cutoff sets how bright it is, the modulation rate and depth decide whether it reads as an instrument or as electronics, and the envelope decides whether it was struck, blown or bowed.

entries.why: These are the settings a synthesis teacher chose to make this instrument recognisable, which makes them a demonstrated starting point rather than a preference. What carries the identification is usually the combination rather than any one value: the cutoff sets how bright it is, the modulation rate and depth decide whether it reads as an instrument or as electronics, and the envelope decides whether it was struck, blown or bowed.

listen_for.sounds_like: a recognisable saxophone rather than a synthesizer imitating one — the test is whether somebody names the instrument without being told
listen_for.confusable_with: the same settings on the wrong source waveform, which lands somewhere adjacent and unconvincing
